findings.quote: Swapping which ratio is called x and which is called r gives √(x/r) instead of √(rx).
findings.note: The correct result √(rx) is symmetric in r and x, so exchanging the two labels leaves it unchanged and cannot produce √(x/r). The stated error does not lead to the option it is attached to. A student who reached √(x/r) divided one of the ratios instead of multiplying it.
findings.fix: Using the radius ratio the wrong way round, R₂/R₁ = 1/r instead of R₁/R₂ = r, in v₁/v₂ = √(g₁R₁/(g₂R₂)) gives √(x/r) instead of √(rx).

notes: Solved independently: v_e = √(2gR), so v₁/v₂ = √(g₁R₁/(g₂R₂)) = √(xr) = √(rx), option 3. All three printed equations are correct and each follows from the one above. Symmetry of √(rx) under exchange of r and x confirmed with sympy.
